summary: Iter26 FRED macro feeds: backend + frontend + regression all passing. 110/110 pytest tests pass (9 new iter26 + 101 regression). Live FRED data confirmed on dashboard widget.

minor.issue: Pre-existing leftover doc with _id='snapshot' (latest=None, fetched_at=2026-06-25T10:47:46) — likely an early-prototype artifact. Does not affect responses (route filters by series_id) but pollutes the collection.

action_items: Optional cleanup: drop the stray db.fred_cache document with _id='snapshot' (legacy artifact).
critical_code_review_comments: macro_feeds.get_macro_snapshot line 116 has dead-code guard `db = _get_db() if 'get_db' not in globals() else get_db()` — since `get_db` IS imported at module level (line 20), the right branch always executes. The left branch is unreachable. Suggest simplifying to `db = get_db()`.
Two redundant `import macro_feeds` statements inside test_get_macro_snapshot_uses_cache (lines 127 & 143) and test_get_macro_snapshot_falls_back_to_stale_cache (lines 158 & 172). Harmless but messy.
_fetch_locks is a module-global dict that grows once per series_id (max 5 entries) — fine, but if SERIES is ever extended dynamically it could leak. Acceptable for current 5-series scope.
Cache TTL/locks survive the process; in a multi-worker uvicorn deploy each worker maintains its own _fetch_locks. Still bounded by 5 FRED calls/worker/hour — acceptable.
